cond_0001.intro:
We are looking for a Postdoctoral Fellow to join our team, working in Biochemistry.
The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
Characteristics of a postdoctoral appointment:
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Perform and assist other research personnel with structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods. Perform and assist other research personnel with measurements of GPCR signaling to assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family. Perform and assist other research personnel with high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes. Perform and assist other research personnel with fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network. Perform and assist other research personnel with computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins. Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories. Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author. Plan, design and execute complex research studies, procedures and protocols. Participate in discovery projects. Coordinate research study activities; lead and manage projects. Oversee organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings. Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts. Participate in meetings with principle investigator and research staff in which you will evaluate/interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures. Maintain supplies, may require negotiation with vendors, and track purchase orders. May oversee the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.
Knowledge – Skills – Abilities
Required knowledge: biology, chemistry, protein structure, GPCR pharmacology, computer programming, mathematics, bioinformatics, statistics, documentation, records management, data utilization, complex problem solving, critical thinking, resource management, and writing skills
Skills and abilities: This will vary based on the hiring manager's preferences and should include things that can be learned or trained for.

PhD in a scientific field
PhD in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular pharmacology, biophysics, structural bioinformatics or structural biology-related discipline
Preferred Requirements
Field: Structural Biology, Computational Biology, Biochemistry or Biophysics
Appropriate experience may be substituted for education on an equivalent basis.

The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
Characteristics of a postdoctoral appointment:
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
People generally become stronger in this kind of structural and computational research over time as they build hands-on experience and learn from feedback in the lab.
cond_0014.responsibilities:
Perform and assist other research personnel with structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods.
Perform and assist other research personnel with measurements of GPCR signaling to assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family.
Perform and assist other research personnel with high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes.
Perform and assist other research personnel with fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network.
Perform and assist other research personnel with computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins.
Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories.
Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author.
Plan, design and execute complex research studies, procedures and protocols.
Participate in discovery projects.
Coordinate research study activities; lead and manage projects.
Oversee organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings.
Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts.
Participate in meetings with principle investigator and research staff in which you will evaluate/interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures.
Maintain supplies, may require negotiation with vendors, and track purchase orders.
May oversee the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.
cond_0014.requirements:
Required knowledge: biology, chemistry, protein structure, GPCR pharmacology, computer programming, mathematics, bioinformatics, statistics, documentation, records management, data utilization, complex problem solving, critical thinking, resource management, and writing skills
Skills and abilities: This will vary based on the hiring manager's preferences and should include things that can be learned or trained for.
Appropriate experience may be substituted for education on an equivalent basis
PhD in a scientific field
PhD in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular pharmacology, biophysics, structural bioinformatics or structural biology-related discipline
Field: Structural Biology, Computational Biology, Biochemistry or Biophysics

cond_0047.intro:
We are looking for a Postdoctoral Fellow to join our team.
The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
Characteristics of a postdoctoral appointment:
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
cond_0047.responsibilities:
Perform and assist other research personnel with structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods.
Perform and assist other research personnel with measurements of GPCR signaling to assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family.
Perform and assist other research personnel with high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes.
Perform and assist other research personnel with fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network.
Perform and assist other research personnel with computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins.
Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories.
Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author.
Plan, design and execute complex research studies, procedures and protocols.
Participate in discovery projects.
Coordinate research study activities; lead and manage projects.
Oversee organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings.
Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts.
Participate in meetings with principle investigator and research staff in which you will evaluate/interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures.
Maintain supplies, may require negotiation with vendors, and track purchase orders.
May oversee the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.
cond_0047.requirements:
PhD in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular pharmacology, biophysics, structural bioinformatics, or a structural biology-related discipline required; advanced degree or additional postdoctoral training strongly preferred.
Demonstrated expertise in Structural Biology, Computational Biology, Biochemistry, or Biophysics.
Deep knowledge of biology, chemistry, and protein structure.
Advanced knowledge of GPCR pharmacology.
Strong command of computer programming, mathematics, and bioinformatics.
Proficiency in statistics, data utilization, and records management.
Proven track record in complex problem solving and critical thinking.
Exceptional scientific writing skills and strong ability to communicate research findings clearly.
Solid understanding of resource management and documentation practices.

cond_0108.intro:
We are looking for a Postdoctoral Fellow to join our team in Biochemistry.
The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
Characteristics of a postdoctoral appointment:
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
cond_0108.responsibilities:
Collaborate with other research personnel on structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods.
Work alongside other research personnel to measure GPCR signaling and assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family.
Coordinate with other research personnel on high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes.
Support other research personnel in fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network.
Assist other research personnel with computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins.
Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories.
Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author.
Plan, design and carry out complex research studies, procedures and protocols in coordination with the team.
Participate in discovery projects.
Coordinate research study activities and help manage projects.
Share responsibility for the organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings.
Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts.
Participate in meetings with the principal investigator and research staff to evaluate and interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures.
Help maintain supplies, coordinate with vendors as needed, and track purchase orders.
May support the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.
cond_0108.requirements:
Appropriate experience may be substituted for education on an equivalent basis
PhD in a scientific field
PhD in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular pharmacology, biophysics, structural bioinformatics or structural biology-related discipline
Field: Structural Biology, Computational Biology, Biochemistry or Biophysics
Required knowledge: biology, chemistry, protein structure, GPCR pharmacology, computer programming, mathematics, bioinformatics, statistics, documentation, records management, data utilization, complex problem solving, critical thinking, resource management, and writing skills

cond_0122.intro:
We're looking for a Postdoctoral Fellow to join our team, working in Biochemistry.
The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
Characteristics of a postdoctoral appointment:
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
People generally become stronger in this kind of structural and computational research over time as they build hands-on experience and learn from feedback in the lab.

Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
A postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPCR pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to pursue a career of his/her own choosing.
Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development.
Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals.
Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research.
Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment.
The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature; the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
cond_0142.responsibilities:
Conduct structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods, and provide technical support to other research personnel as needed.
Carry out measurements of GPCR signaling to assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family, and support other research personnel with the same.
Perform high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes, and assist other research personnel with related tasks.
Contribute to fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network, and support other research personnel with related work.
Conduct computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins, and assist other research personnel as required.
Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories.
Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author.
Plan, design and execute complex research studies, procedures and protocols.
Contribute to discovery projects.
Coordinate research study activities; lead and manage projects.
Oversee organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings.
Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts.
Attend meetings with the principal investigator and research staff to evaluate and interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures.
Maintain supplies, handle vendor negotiations as required, and track purchase orders.
May oversee the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.
cond_0142.requirements:
PhD in a scientific field, preferably in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular pharmacology, biophysics, structural bioinformatics, or a structural biology-related discipline.
Field of study: Structural Biology, Computational Biology, Biochemistry, or Biophysics.
Knowledge of biology, chemistry, protein structure, GPCR pharmacology, computer programming, mathematics, bioinformatics, statistics, documentation, records management, data utilization, complex problem solving, critical thinking, resource management, and scientific writing.
Appropriate experience may be substituted for education on an equivalent basis.

cond_0226.intro:
We are looking for a Postdoctoral Fellow to join our team, working in Biochemistry.
The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
Characteristics of a postdoctoral appointment:
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
cond_0226.responsibilities:
Perform and assist other research personnel with structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods.
Perform and assist other research personnel with measurements of GPCR signaling to assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family.
Perform and assist other research personnel with high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes.
Perform and assist other research personnel with fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network.
Perform and assist other research personnel with computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins.
Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories.
Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author.
Plan, design and execute complex research studies, procedures and protocols.
Participate in discovery projects.
Coordinate research study activities; lead and manage projects.
Oversee organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings.
Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts.
Participate in meetings with principle investigator and research staff in which you will evaluate/interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures.
Maintain supplies, may require negotiation with vendors, and track purchase orders.
May oversee the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.
Knowledge – Skills – Abilities
Required knowledge: biology, chemistry, protein structure, GPCR pharmacology, computer programming, mathematics, bioinformatics, statistics, documentation, records management, data utilization, complex problem solving, critical thinking, resource management, and writing skills
Skills and abilities: This will vary based on the hiring manager's preferences and should include things that can be learned or trained for.

Appropriate experience may be substituted for education on an equivalent basis
PhD in a scientific field
PhD in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular pharmacology, biophysics, structural bioinformatics or structural biology-related discipline
Field: Structural Biology, Computational Biology, Biochemistry or Biophysics

cond_0239.intro:
We are looking for a Postdoctoral Fellow to join our team in Biochemistry at [Company name masked].
The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
People typically grow stronger in this kind of structural and computational research over time as they build hands-on experience and learn from feedback in the lab.
cond_0239.responsibilities:
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
Perform and assist other research personnel with structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods. Perform and assist other research personnel with measurements of GPCR signaling to assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family. Perform and assist other research personnel with high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes. Perform and assist other research personnel with fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network. Perform and assist other research personnel with computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins. Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories. Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author. Plan, design and execute complex research studies, procedures and protocols. Participate in discovery projects. Coordinate research study activities; lead and manage projects. Oversee organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings. Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts. Participate in meetings with principle investigator and research staff in which you will evaluate/interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures. Maintain supplies, may require negotiation with vendors, and track purchase orders. May oversee the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.
Required knowledge: biology, chemistry, protein structure, GPCR pharmacology, computer programming, mathematics, bioinformatics, statistics, documentation, records management, data utilization, complex problem solving, critical thinking, resource management, and writing skills

The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
Characteristics of a postdoctoral appointment:
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
cond_0252.responsibilities:
Collaborate with other research personnel on structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods.
Work alongside other research personnel to measure GPCR signaling and assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family.
Coordinate with other research personnel on high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes.
Support other research personnel in fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network.
Assist other research personnel with computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins.
Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories.
Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author.
Plan, design and carry out complex research studies, procedures and protocols in coordination with the team.
Participate in discovery projects.
Coordinate research study activities and help manage projects.
Share responsibility for the organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings.
Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts.
Participate in meetings with the principal investigator and research staff to evaluate and interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures.
Help maintain supplies, coordinate with vendors as needed, and track purchase orders.
May support the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.
cond_0252.requirements:
Appropriate experience may be substituted for education on an equivalent basis
PhD in a scientific field
PhD in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular pharmacology, biophysics, structural bioinformatics or structural biology-related discipline
Field: Structural Biology, Computational Biology, Biochemistry or Biophysics
Required knowledge: biology, chemistry, protein structure, GPCR pharmacology, computer programming, mathematics, bioinformatics, statistics, documentation, records management, data utilization, complex problem solving, critical thinking, resource management, and writing skills
cond_0252.values: We value high performance and work that reflects care, discipline, and strong judgment. We believe results matter, and so does the standard behind them.

cond_0278.intro:
The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing.
Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development.
Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals.
Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research.
Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment.
The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature; the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
cond_0278.responsibilities:
Lead structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods, and direct other research personnel in this work.
Execute measurements of GPCR signaling to assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family, and guide other research personnel in these efforts.
Drive high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes, overseeing contributions from other research personnel.
Spearhead fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network, and direct other research personnel in related tasks.
Lead computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins, and direct other research personnel accordingly.
Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories.
Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author.
Plan, design and execute complex research studies, procedures and protocols.
Own discovery projects and take accountability for their progress.
Direct research study activities; lead and manage projects.
Oversee organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings.
Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts.
Lead meetings with the principal investigator and research staff to evaluate and interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures.
Manage supplies, negotiate with vendors as needed, and track purchase orders.
May oversee the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.
Required knowledge: biology, chemistry, protein structure, GPCR pharmacology, computer programming, mathematics, bioinformatics, statistics, documentation, records management, data utilization, complex problem solving, critical thinking, resource management, and writing skills
cond_0278.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD in a scientific field
Field: Structural Biology, Computational Biology, Biochemistry or Biophysics
Preferred Requirements
PhD in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular pharmacology, biophysics, structural bioinformatics or structural biology-related discipline
Appropriate experience may be substituted for education on an equivalent basis.

Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
cond_0312.responsibilities:
Perform and actively collaborate with other research personnel on structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods.
Perform and actively collaborate with other research personnel on measurements of GPCR signaling to assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family.
Perform and actively collaborate with other research personnel on high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes.
Perform and actively collaborate with other research personnel on fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network.
Perform and actively collaborate with other research personnel on computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins.
Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories.
Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author.
Plan, design and execute complex research studies, procedures and protocols.
Actively contribute to discovery projects.
Coordinate research study activities; lead and manage projects, regularly connecting with team members to align on priorities.
Oversee organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings.
Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts.
Participate in regular meetings with the principal investigator and research staff, actively contributing to discussions where you will evaluate/interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures.
Maintain supplies, may require negotiation with vendors, and track purchase orders.
May oversee the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.
cond_0312.requirements:
Required knowledge: biology, chemistry, protein structure, GPCR pharmacology, computer programming, mathematics, bioinformatics, statistics, documentation, records management, data utilization, complex problem solving, critical thinking, resource management, and writing skills
Minimum Requirements
PhD in a scientific field
PhD in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular pharmacology, biophysics, structural bioinformatics or structural biology-related discipline
Preferred Requirements
Field focus in Structural Biology, Computational Biology, Biochemistry or Biophysics
Appropriate experience may be substituted for education on an equivalent basis

cond_0333.intro:
The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing.
Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development.
Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals.
Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research.
Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment.
The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature; the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
cond_0333.responsibilities:
Work alongside other research personnel on structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods.
Collaborate with other research personnel on measurements of GPCR signaling to assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family.
Support other research personnel with high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes.
Work with other research personnel on fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network.
Assist other research personnel with computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins.
Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories.
Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author.
Plan, design and carry out complex research studies, procedures and protocols in coordination with the team.
Participate in discovery projects.
Help coordinate research study activities and contribute to project management.
Share responsibility for the organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings.
Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts.
Participate in meetings with the principal investigator and research staff to evaluate and interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures.
Maintain supplies, may require coordination with vendors, and track purchase orders.
May support the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.
Required knowledge: biology, chemistry, protein structure, GPCR pharmacology, computer programming, mathematics, bioinformatics, statistics, documentation, records management, data utilization, complex problem solving, critical thinking, resource management, and writing skills
cond_0333.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD in a scientific field
Background in Structural Biology, Computational Biology, Biochemistry or Biophysics
Preferred Requirements
PhD in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular pharmacology, biophysics, structural bioinformatics or structural biology-related discipline
Appropriate experience may be substituted for education on an equivalent basis.

Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
A postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPCR pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to pursue a career of his/her own choosing.
Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development.
Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals.
Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research.
Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment.
The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature; the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
cond_0367.responsibilities:
Conduct structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy, and other biophysical and biochemical methods; provide technical support to other research personnel on these methods as needed.
Carry out measurements of GPCR signaling to assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family; support other research personnel with these measurements as required.
Execute high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes; assist other research personnel with modeling tasks as needed.
Conduct fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network; support other research personnel with related tasks.
Perform computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins; assist other research personnel as required.
Deposit structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories to disseminate research results.
Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author.
Plan, design, and execute complex research studies, procedures, and protocols.
Contribute to discovery projects.
Coordinate research study activities; lead and manage projects.
Oversee organization, synthesis, and analysis of data and findings.
Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings, and scientific manuscripts.
Attend meetings with the principal investigator and research staff to evaluate and interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures.
Maintain supplies, track purchase orders, and handle vendor negotiations as needed.
May oversee laboratory personnel, including training and development, daily work direction, delegation, and establishing priorities.
cond_0367.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD in a scientific field
PhD in chemistry, biochemistry, molecular pharmacology, biophysics, structural bioinformatics, or a structural biology-related discipline
Background in structural biology, computational biology, biochemistry, or biophysics
Preferred Requirements
Knowledge of biology, chemistry, protein structure, GPCR pharmacology, computer programming, mathematics, bioinformatics, statistics, documentation, records management, data utilization, complex problem solving, critical thinking, resource management, and scientific writing

cond_0381.intro:
We are looking for a Postdoctoral Fellow to join our team.
The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
Characteristics of a postdoctoral appointment:
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).
cond_0381.responsibilities:
Perform and assist other research personnel with structure-function studies of chemokine-GPCR complexes using NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography, cryoelectron microscopy and other biophysical and biochemical methods.
Perform and assist other research personnel with measurements of GPCR signaling to assess the presence of and structural origins of biased agonism in the chemokine family.
Perform and assist other research personnel with high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes.
Perform and assist other research personnel with fragment-based drug discovery targeting the chemokine network.
Perform and assist other research personnel with computational design and experimental characterization of novel metamorphic or fold-switching proteins.
Disseminate research results by depositing structures and data in the protein data bank or other public repositories.
Prepare research results for publication in peer-reviewed journals as primary author or co-author.
Plan, design and execute complex research studies, procedures and protocols.
Participate in discovery projects.
Coordinate research study activities; lead and manage projects.
Oversee organization, synthesis and analysis of data and findings.
Prepare scientific reports, outcome findings and scientific manuscripts.
Participate in meetings with principle investigator and research staff in which you will evaluate/interpret the validity of data, develop methodologies, and design and evaluate lab procedures.
Maintain supplies, may require negotiation with vendors, and track purchase orders.
May oversee the work of laboratory personnel including training and development as well as daily work direction, delegation and establishing priorities.

cond_0424.intro:
We are looking for a Postdoctoral Fellow to join our team, working in Biochemistry.
The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
Characteristics of a postdoctoral appointment:
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).

cond_0438.intro:
The Volkman laboratory conducts NIH grant-supported research in several areas of chemokine biology, with an emphasis on the structural details of chemokine proteins, their interactions with cell surface receptors, and novel approaches to modify their functions in vivo with small molecule or engineered protein ligands. Actively funded projects with multiple years of future grant support focus on 1) the structural basis of chemokine function, with the goal of developing a comprehensive structure-function atlas of the chemokine network of the human immune system; 2) fragment-based development of small molecule inhibitors of CCL28, a chemokine implicated in pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer; and 3) the thermodynamic origins of metamorphic folding in the human chemokine XCL1. Additional project details can be found in the NIH Reporter database.
According to the National Institute of Health (NIH) and the National Science Foundation (NSF), a postdoc is an individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced research training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue his or her chosen career path. In addition, according to the National Postdoc Association (NPA), Postdoctoral appointees can pursue basic, clinical or translational projects so long as their primary effort is devoted toward their own scholarship. Postdocs are essential to the scholarly mission of the mentor and host institution, and thus are expected to have the freedom to publish the results of their scholarship.
Recent PhD graduates or those anticipating the completion of the PhD degree in the next 12 months in a scientific discipline related to structural biology, computational biology, molecular biophysics, or GPRC pharmacology with an interest in any of the aforementioned projects are encouraged to apply.
It is expected that postdocs at [Company name masked], with the assistance of their supervisor, will:
Transition to career independence through the development of professional skills that enable the postdoc to actively pursue a career of his/her own choosing. Be supervised by at least one senior scholar who actively promotes the postdoc's professional development. Establish an individual development plan (IDP) that incorporates equally the postdoc's career and training goals and the mentor's research goals. Pursue basic, clinical, or translational projects so long as effort is focused primarily on research. Publish results of the postdoc's research and scholarship during their appointment. The postdoctoral appointment is temporary by nature, the aggregate amount of time spent as a postdoc is recommended to not exceed five years (not including family medical leave or maternity/paternity leave).

Perform and actively collaborate with other research personnel on high-throughput computational modeling of chemokine-GPCR complexes.
